method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Infection is the likeliest cause** in neonates (<28 days corrected age) and young infants (<3 months), but other serious conditions can look the same at first.
claims.source_text: Infections are the most likely cause of illness in neonates (<28 days corrected age) and young infants (<3 months), however several other serious conditions can have similar initial presentations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A fever in any neonate (≥38°C) warrants investigation and empiric IV antibiotics.**
claims.source_text: A fever in any neonate (≥38°C) warrants initial investigation and empiric IV antibiotics
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever is not always present** — temperature may be normal or low (<36.5°C). Observation, serial examination and investigations often help. **Early senior review is essential.**
claims.source_text: Fever is not always present. Neonates and young infants can present with a normal or low temperature (<36.5°C) … Unwell infants can present with non-specific findings and may not have a fever; a period of observation, serial examinations and investigations are often helpful Early review by senior clinician is essential
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **UTI is the most common bacterial infection.** Highest-risk babies: low birth weight or premature, known medical condition (e.g. congenital anomaly), socially disadvantaged families.
claims.source_text: Infection is the most common cause of illness, with urinary tract infections (see UTI) being the most common bacterial infection … Low birth weight and premature babies Those with a known medical condition eg congenital anomaly Babies from socially disadvantaged families
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about:** irritability, fever, lethargy or sleepiness, **poor feeding (<50% of normal over the previous 24 hours)**, **urine output (<4 wet nappies in 24 hours)**, vomiting (especially bilious), apnoea, BRUE or seizures.
claims.source_text: Irritability Fever Lethargy or increased sleepiness Poor feeding (volume taken in previous 24 hours <50% of normal) Urine output (<4 wet nappies in 24 hours) Vomiting, particularly bilious Apnoea History of brief resolved unexplained event (BRUE) or seizures
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Birth history:** prematurity, maternal GBS colonisation, perinatal stress, prolonged rupture of membranes, maternal fever, Apgars and resuscitation, postnatal antibiotics, vitamin K.
claims.source_text: Birth history: prematurity, maternal Group B strep (GBS) colonisation, perinatal stress, prolonged rupture of membranes, maternal fever, Apgars and resuscitation requirements, history of postnatal investigations and antibiotics, vitamin K after birth
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also:** previous child with early onset sepsis, immunodeficiency, sick contacts, **HSV exposure**, and **high parental concern**.
claims.source_text: Family history: previous child with early onset sepsis, history of immunodeficiency Immunisation history Sick contacts Exposure to herpes simplex virus High level of parental concern
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Behaviour and appearance are the best guide** to whether serious illness is likely.
claims.source_text: General aspects of the neonate or young infant's behaviour and appearance provide the best indication of whether serious illness is likely
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Breathing:** grunting, tachypnoea, increased work of breathing, hypoxia, apnoea, chest deformity.
claims.source_text: Breathing Grunting Tachypnoea Increased work of breathing Hypoxia Apnoea Any chest deformity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Circulation:** pallor, mottling, cyanosis; tachy- or bradycardia; **central capillary refill ≥3 seconds**; murmur, weak or reduced femoral pulses, enlarged liver; weight gain from fluid overload; hypotension.
claims.source_text: Circulation Colour: pallor, mottling, cyanosis Tachycardia or bradycardia Central capillary refill time ≥3 seconds Cardiac murmur, weak peripheral pulses, enlarged liver, reduced femoral pulses Increased weight gain (fluid overload) Hypotension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Disability/neuro:** lethargy, poor feeding, irritability, not responding to social cues, difficult to wake, weak/high-pitched/continuous cry, reduced tone, abnormal movements, focal signs, focal/complex/prolonged seizures.
claims.source_text: Disability/neuro Lethargy or decreased activity Poor feeding Irritability Not responding normally to social cues Difficult to wake Weak, high-pitched or continuous cry Reduced tone Abnormal movements Focal neurological signs Focal, complex or prolonged seizures
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haematological:** non-blanching rash, bruising, bleeding. **Infection:** fever or hypothermia, bulging fontanelle, neck stiffness, **vesicular rash or encephalopathy (HSV)**.
claims.source_text: Haematological Non-blanching rash Bruising Bleeding Infection Fever or hypothermia Bulging fontanelle Neck stiffness Vesicular rash, encephalopathy (HSV)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Primary HSV in the first month:** skin vesicles (absent in 1/3 of neonates, who can be afebrile), seizures or encephalopathy.
claims.source_text: Primary HSV, in first 1 month of life Skin vesicles (not present in 1/3 of neonates and can be afebrile), seizures or encephalopathy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Malrotation with volvulus:** bile-stained vomit, abdominal distension.
claims.source_text: Malrotation with volvulus Bile-stained vomit, abdominal distension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pyloric stenosis:** progressive, non-bilious projectile vomiting, olive mass, hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis. **Intussusception:** intermittent severe pain, vomiting, pallor, lethargy, rectal bleeding (red currant stool is late).
claims.source_text: Pyloric stenosis Progressive, non-bilious and projectile vomiting, pyloric olive-shaped mass, hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis … Intussusception Intermittent severe abdominal pain, vomiting, pallor, lethargy and rectal bleeding (red currant stool, a late sign)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **NEC:** abdominal distension, tenderness, vomiting, blood in stool, abdominal wall discolouration or erythema.
claims.source_text: Necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) Abdominal distention, tenderness, vomiting, blood in stool, discolouration or erythema of abdominal wall
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Congenital heart disease:** cyanosis, murmur (not always), sweating with feeds, cardiac failure, poor or absent peripheral pulses. **SVT:** persistent marked tachycardia, pallor, poor feeding.
claims.source_text: Congenital cardiac disease Cyanosis, murmur (not always present), diaphoresis (sweating) with feeding, cardiac failure (tachypnoea, enlarged liver, hypoperfusion), poor or absent peripheral pulses Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and other arrhythmias Persistent marked tachycardia, pallor, poor feeding
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Congenital adrenal hyperplasia:** ambiguous genitalia, hypotension, dehydration, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia. **Non-accidental injury:** bruising, unexplained injury, intracranial injury, neglect.
claims.source_text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia Ambiguous genitalia, hypotension, dehydration, hyponatraemia, and hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia … Non-accidental injury (NAI) Child abuse Bruising, unexplained injury, signs of intracranial injury, signs of neglect
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unwell neonate or young infant:** BGL, VBG if available, FBE, UEC, LFT, CRP, blood culture, urine MCS (SPA).
claims.source_text: For unwell neonates and young infants: Perform BGL, consider VBG if available, FBE, UEC, LFT, CRP, blood culture, urine MCS (see SPA)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lumbar puncture in neonates <28 days unless contraindicated; consider it in young infants.**
claims.source_text: Lumbar puncture in neonates <28 days (if not contraindicated), consider in young infants
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **By likely cause, consider** ammonia, viral swabs (e.g. HSV), ECG, and CXR, abdominal or neuroimaging.
claims.source_text: Ammonia level Viral swabs eg HSV ECG Consider imaging, depending on the cause CXR Abdominal imaging Neuroimaging
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every seriously unwell neonate or young infant:** prompt sepsis management with **early empiric antibiotics (IV/IM/intraosseous)**, aciclovir if indicated, adequate analgesia and sedation.
claims.source_text: All seriously unwell neonates and young infants should receive: Prompt management of sepsis with early administration of empiric antibiotics (IV/IM/intraosseous) Aciclovir if indicated Adequate analgesia and sedation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fluids:** resuscitate as required; maintenance accounting for oral intake; **restrict to two-thirds of maintenance in meningitis or respiratory infection**; judicious in cardiac causes.
claims.source_text: Fluid resuscitation as required Maintenance fluids, account for oral intake Restrict fluid rate in meningitis or respiratory infections to two-thirds of maintenance rate Judicious fluid management in cardiac causes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected bowel obstruction: nasogastric tube on free drainage.**
claims.source_text: Nasogastric tube on free drainage if bowel obstruction is suspected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected duct-dependent congenital heart disease in a neonate: discuss early with cardiology/ICU/retrieval and consider IV prostaglandin.**
claims.source_text: In neonates with suspected duct dependent congenital cardiac condition, early discussion with cardiology/ICU/retrieval team, consider IV prostaglandin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve a senior clinician early and refer early** to paediatric, surgical or sub-specialist teams as indicated.
claims.source_text: Involve senior clinician Early referral to paediatric, surgical and/or sub-specialist team as indicated
